name: shoco
baseline: smaz (short-string compressor); also gzip and xz command-line tools
workload: Compress and decompress English words: all words in /usr/dict/share/words versus smaz, and /usr/share/dict/words (4,953,680 bytes) compressed as one file with the included shoco command-line tool versus gzip and xz.
claimed_speedup: README: shoco 'is typically faster by at least a factor of 2' than smaz; example 0.325s (smaz, 28% average compression) versus 0.145s (shoco, 33% average compression) for compress plus decompress of all words in /usr/dict/share/words (about 2.2x, derived from page data). Versus gzip and xz on /usr/share/dict/words: shoco 0.070s compress / 0.010s decompress / 3,393,975 bytes; gzip 0.470s / 0.048s / 1,476,083 bytes (6.7x and 4.8x faster, derived from page data); xz 3.300s / 0.148s / 1,229,980 bytes (47x and 15x faster, derived from page data).
tradeoffs: Entropy coder for short ASCII strings built on a compiled-in bigram model (default model tuned for English words; a Python script generates new models from your own data). Compression ratio is far worse than gzip or xz on larger inputs (3.39 MB versus 1.48 MB and 1.23 MB on the 4.95 MB word list); output never grows for plain ASCII input but non-ASCII input can; copy-in C files (shoco.c, shoco.h, shoco_model.h), no packaging.
caveats: First-party numbers measured 'on my computer': no CPU, compiler, flags or OS version stated, no timing method or run count, and the smaz row has no committed harness. The gzip/xz table times the shoco command-line tool on one whole 4.95 MB file, which the README itself calls 'not a strong point of shoco', so it does not measure the short-string use case, and gzip/xz are generic compressors with much better ratios, so the speed comparison is not like for like. The baseline is not a C++ standard facility. The README begins 'This project is unmaintained. You should use ZStandard nowadays'; the last code changes in the commit list are from 2015 (merge of pull request #17 on 2015-12-08), and the 2026-02-16 commit is titled 'project is unmaintained'. A third-party benchmark snippet found by search covers a Go port (tmthrgd/shoco), not this C code, and was not opened.
found_via: seed-record pass: awesome-c Compression listing 'Compressor for small text strings' (https://github.com/oz123/awesome-c, listing page not opened); evidence read from the repo page, README.md, LICENSE and commit list on github.com
